newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares fleetingly set a fresh trading high on Tuesday before settling back to end a whisker below a new closing record, held back by lacklustre performances from some internationals after the dollar stalled.

"We could have just scraped to another record if one or two of the internationals had held up a bit better," said one dealer, observing the market appeared content to churn around Monday's record high closing levels for a while.
The AEX share index closed 0.03 points easier at 576.93 with an earlier attempt to break higher snuffed out rapidly after the index brushed to a new trading high of 577.36.
Dealers said there were signs of plentiful overhead supply at yesterday's record with investors wanting to see the market consolidating after a recent rise.

"It's a reasonable development in the market," said a dealer. "The market has expected a small technical rebound after some days of going up. Volumes are low again but we see support kicking in around the old high of 572.50."

"Underlying all this the market sentiment is still pretty good, although people are worrying about the direction of interest rates," said another dealer. "Also we'd have expected a bit more positive response to today's bond market gains."
Dealers said markets were becoming convinced pressure was building for a U.S. interest rate rise, although political considerations in the U.S. might be holding off such a move.

"People are beginning to be a bit worried. Rates really should have gone up by now but I think that might not happen until the U.S. elections in November," said a dealer. "If I was an investor I'd want to stand back from the market now."

U.S. figures due later in the week could set the tone on Wall Street and give the green light for another attempt to reach new Dutch highs. "The unemployment figures on Friday might give us a new impulse," said a trader.

The publishers modestly followed up Monday's strong gains on buying related to a new instrument issued by Rabobank. The bank's "Sprinter" combines a bond issue and an index of four publishers, Wolters Kluwer, VNU, Polygram and Elsevier.
Dealers said the Sprinter's mechanism allowed investors to leverage up capital gains in the publishers' share prices.
"The publishers did very well yesterday, helping the whole market in fact, because Rabobank had to go out and buy the shares to cover their new deal," said one.
Wolters Kluwer extended Monday's 7.80 guilder gain with a fresh 1.60 guilder advance to 216.90 guilders.

Fresh demand in cyclicals shares saw Akzo 2.70 guilders higher at 210.10 and DSM 3.00 guilders higher at 171.00. Hoogovens put on 1.40 guilders to 62.70, fuelled by talk of a broker's upgrade and reports of increasing steel consumption.
Retailer Ahold closed 0.70 guilders higher at 97.60 guilders, responding positively to news of its new Spanish food joint venture and the takeover of 10 supermarkets in Madrid.

Heineken finished 3.30 guilders down at 309.20 and Unilever lost 70 cents to 269.40, cited by some dealers as key declines which held the AEX back from a new closing record. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
